newsitem.title: UK: Stocks soar in London, Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Stocks soar in London, Tokyo.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - Leading shares soared to record levels amid euphoria over the new Labour party government's decision to grant the Bank of England freedom to set interest rates without political interference.
The FTSE 100 Index closed 63.7 points higher at a record closing level of 4,519.3.

FRANKFURT - The German share market ended bourse trade at a record closing high, powered ahead by record overnight gains in the United States and Japan and well-received results from top companies. The blue-chip DAX index pared its early gains to close at 3,568.28, up 39.50 points, or 1.12 percent. In post-bourse trade the DAX stood at 3,548.52, down 17.17 points.
PARIS - French stocks fell on polls suggesting a close parliamentary election between the ruling conservatives and the Socialists.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 20.91 points or 0.78 percent at 2,651.93 after losing its early gains triggered by a sharp rise on Wall Street on Monday.

ZURICH - Swiss shares broke from their recent record run to end below the 5,000 point-level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) after Nestle's first quarter results triggered profit-taking on a broad front.
The SMI slipped 41.2 points, or 0.82 percent, to end at 4,988.4 and the broad Swiss Performance Index dropped 19.79 points, or 0.62 percent, to 3,150.77.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market returned from a long holiday weekend in a bullish mood, with the benchmark index powering above the closely watched 20,000 point barrier for the first time since mid-December. Brokers said a buying binge by foreign investors combined with pension fund purchases to fuel a hefty gain of over three percent.
The 225-share Nikkei average jumped 666.17 points or 3.41 percent to finish at 20,180.92, the highest closing level since 20,413.46 set on December 17.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks continued their powerful advance for the fifth day Tuesday, closing on hefty gains as Monday's record highs on Wall Street swept local prices higher. The Hang Seng Index jumped 180.00 points, or 1.34 percent, to 13,579.34. The index hit an intra-day high of 13,679.92, the first time it has been above 13,600 points since late February.

SYDNEY - Australian stocks closed at a record high after a fresh high on Wall Street and strong rises in other markets in the Asia Pacific region encouraged investors. The All Ordinaries index ended 20.1 points higher at 2,512.8 after earlier hitting a new intra-day high of 2,518.5.

JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's all-share index rose to a record closing high despite industrial shares being knocked off their highs by expectations of a weaker Wall Street opening. Gold shares ended slightly firmer after bullion gained $3 on Monday. But dealers said volumes were thin and players were concerned that the rise in the bullion price could not be sustained.
The All-share index rose 21.6 points to a new high of 7,212.0 points, the industrial index was up 5.3 points to 8,568.7 points and the gold index added 6.6 points to 1,212.3 points.
